reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Scope and definition of practice of pharmacy
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 1 and subdivisions (1) to (10): defines practice of pharmacy including prescription orders, medication therapeutic plans, compounding and dispensing, vaccine ordering and administration (with listed disease exclusions and age thresholds), drug selection and reviews, safe storage and records, consultation, nicotine replacement under § 338.665, HIV postexposure prophylaxis under § 338.730, and pharmacy operations. Source notes record enactments through 2026 and a severability reference to § 1.1009.

headings.title: Licensure requirement for pharmacy practice
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 2: prohibits any person from engaging in the practice of pharmacy unless licensed under the provisions of this chapter.

headings.title: Auxiliary personnel supervision and pharmacist liability
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 3: permits use of auxiliary personnel under direct supervision of a pharmacist to assist in duties; specifies that auxiliary assistance does not relieve pharmacist of statutory compliance and establishes pharmacist responsibility for auxiliary actions.

headings.title: Exceptions for prescribing practitioners and optometrists
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 4: establishes that chapter does not prohibit or interfere with registered practitioners of medicine, dentistry, podiatry, veterinary medicine (animals only), or optometry (§§ 195.070, 336.220) compounding, administering, prescribing, or dispensing own prescriptions.

headings.title: Medication therapy services under physician protocol
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 5: authorizes a pharmacist holding a certificate of medication therapeutic plan authority to provide medication therapy services pursuant to a written physician-approved protocol.

headings.title: Pharmacy ownership with pharmacist in charge
headings.reviewNote: Verified subsection 6: section does not prevent any person, firm, or corporation from owning a pharmacy under §§ 338.210–338.315, provided a licensed pharmacist is in charge. Revised title to include the pharmacist-in-charge condition.

headings.title: Sale of nonprescription drugs and ordinary remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 7: clarifies that section does not apply to or interfere with retail sales of nonprescription drugs or ordinary household remedies by non-pharmacists.

headings.title: Health carrier protocol requirement prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 8: prohibits health carriers defined in chapter 376 from requiring contracted physicians to enter into written protocols with pharmacists.

headings.title: Diagnosis and independent prescribing prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 9: explicitly limits section by providing that it shall not be construed to allow a pharmacist to diagnose or independently prescribe pharmaceuticals.

headings.title: Joint rulemaking for medication therapeutic plans
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 10: authorizes state board of registration for the healing arts and state board of pharmacy to jointly promulgate rules governing protocol requirements and therapeutic plan guidelines under chapter 536.

headings.title: Grant and requirements of therapeutic plan certificate
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 11: authorizes state board of pharmacy to grant certificate of medication therapeutic plan authority to licensed pharmacists meeting board-established education, experience, and fee requirements.

headings.title: Designing and initiating plans under physician protocol
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 12: permits certificate-holding pharmacist to design, initiate, implement, and monitor physician-specific medication therapeutic plans within the scope of the authorizing physician's practice.

headings.title: Therapeutic substitutions without prescription prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 13: clarifies that section does not allow a pharmacist to make therapeutic substitutions without specific physician prescription or protocol authorization.

headings.title: Veterinarian titles and degree definitions
headings.reviewNote: Verified subsection 14: defines listed veterinarian titles/abbreviations by veterinary degree from an accredited school or AVMA ECFVG (printed "EDFVG") certificate. Revised note to match printed text rather than chapter 340 licensure.

headings.title: Vaccine administration protocols and patient observation
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 15 and subdivisions (1)-(2): mandates vaccine administration by protocol in accordance with CDC treatment guidelines and requires requesting patient to remain in pharmacy for a safe observation period.

headings.title: Additional vaccine training requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 16: requires pharmacist to receive additional board-required training before ordering or administering vaccines.

headings.title: ShowMeVax reporting notice and required information
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 17 and subdivisions (1)-(6): mandates informing patient that vaccine administration will be entered into ShowMeVax and lists required reported data fields.

headings.title: Vaccines during declared public health emergency
headings.reviewNote: Verified subsection 18: licensed pharmacist may order and administer FDA-approved or authorized vaccines as lawfully authorized by state or federal government during a state or federally declared public health emergency. Revised title and note to match text.

headings.reviewNote: Verified subsection 1: pharmacist with medication therapeutic plan certificate may provide influenza, group A streptococcus, and COVID-19 medication therapy services pursuant to joint board rules (not general acute respiratory conditions or physician protocol as drafted).

headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 2: directs board of pharmacy and healing arts board to jointly promulgate rules governing pharmacist prescribing and dispensing of nicotine products.

headings.title: Third-party payment for nicotine therapy not mandated
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 3: clarifies that section does not mandate third-party insurance reimbursement for services.

headings.title: Rulemaking validity and nonseverability clause

headings.title: Rx Cares for Missouri Program created in board
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 1: creates Rx Cares for Missouri Program to promote medication safety, disposal, and abuse prevention. Source notes show amendments through 2026.

headings.title: Board authority to allocate funds for program goals
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 2: authorizes board, in consultation with department of mental health, to award grants and expend funds for medication safety programs.

headings.title: Board administration of program in consultation with department
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 3: designates board as administrative agency responsible for program implementation with mental health department.

headings.title: Annual program evaluation report to governor and assembly
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 4: requires board to prepare and submit annual evaluation report to governor and general assembly.

headings.title: Pharmacist dispensing of HIV postexposure prophylaxis
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 1: authorizes licensed pharmacists to dispense HIV postexposure prophylaxis under protocol with physician.

headings.title: Definition of postexposure prophylaxis
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 2: defines postexposure prophylaxis as FDA-approved drugs preventing HIV infection following potential exposure.

headings.title: Definition of CDC guidelines for HIV prophylaxis
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 3: defines CDC guidelines as current clinical recommendations published by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

headings.title: Joint rulemaking for HIV prophylaxis protocols
headings.reviewNote: Read subsection 4: directs healing arts and pharmacy boards to jointly promulgate rules governing protocols for HIV prophylaxis.
